description: A small, fast HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 server engine you build into Rust programs: its own TLS 1.3, no tokio, nothing but the Rust standard library; the HTTP engine of Cameleer and a Cameleering project.
rules: Add simoom with `cargo add simoom` (Rust 1.89 or later). The defaults are HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and WebSocket; for HTTP/1.1 only use `simoom = { version = "0.1", default-features = false, features = ["http1"] }`.

TLS needs the `tls` feature and HTTP/3 the `http3` feature; `full` turns on every protocol including both. compression, cors, auth, cookies, multipart, conditional, websocket-h2 and websocket-h3 are not in `full`; add them by name.

There is no async, no `.await` and no tokio: simoom needs no async runtime and depends on nothing outside the Rust standard library. A service is a plain `Fn(&mut Request<'_>, Reply<'_>) -> Outcome + Send + Sync + 'static`.
Start a server with `Server::builder().listen("0.0.0.0:8080").service(svc).start()?`, which returns a `ServerHandle`; then `server.join()`, or `server.stop(grace)` followed by `join()`.

A service runs on the event-loop thread and must not block (no database calls, file I/O, HTTP calls or sleeps). Move slow work off the loop with `simoom::blocking(|req: OwnedRequest| Response)`, `reply.offload(...)`, or `let r = reply.defer();` answered later with `r.send(response)` from another thread, returning `Outcome::Deferred`.

Finish every `Reply` exactly once (`body`, `body_static`, `empty`, `send`, `fixed`, ...); a dropped reply sends 500. Request accessors return bytes: compare `req.method()` with `b"GET"`, use `path_str()` and `param_str()` for text.
The HTTP client is the separate, blocking `simoom-client` crate; never call it on the loop thread.

simoom is a library, not a web server: there is no static-file server, reverse proxy or config file. QUIC and TLS 0-RTT are refused by design. It needs the standard library and an OS (Linux, Windows, macOS); it is not `no_std`.
Read docs/guides/coding-agents.md for the full rules, the API cheat sheet and a starter program.
